source_sentences.T0: Self-Training without Reranking for Parser Domain Adaptation and Its Impact on Semantic Role Labeling
source_sentences.A0: AbstractWe compare self-training with and without reranking for parser domain adaptation, and examine the impact of syntactic parser adaptation on a semantic role labeling system.
source_sentences.A1: Although self-training without reranking has been found not to improve in-domain accuracy for parsers trained on the WSJ Penn Treebank, we show that it is surprisingly effective for parser domain adaptation.
source_sentences.A2: We also show that simple self-training of a syntactic parser improves out-of-domain accuracy of a semantic role labeler.

source_sentences.T0: All You Need is "Love": Evading Hate-speech Detection
source_sentences.A0: ABSTRACTWith the spread of social networks and their unfortunate use for hate speech, automatic detection of the la er has become a pressing problem.
source_sentences.A1: In this paper, we reproduce seven state-of-the-art hate speech detection models from prior work, and show that they perform well only when tested on the same type of data they were trained on.
source_sentences.A2: Based on these results, we argue that for successful hate speech detection, model architecture is less important than the type of data and labeling criteria.
source_sentences.A3: We further show that all proposed detection techniques are bri le against adversaries who can (automatically) insert typos, change word boundaries or add innocuous words to the original hate speech.
source_sentences.A4: A combination of these methods is also effective against Google Perspective -a cu ingedge solution from industry.
source_sentences.A5: Our experiments demonstrate that adversarial training does not completely mitigate the a acks, and using character-level features makes the models systematically more a ack-resistant than using word-level features.

source_sentences.T0: Study of the Brain Waves for the differentiation of Gamers category between a Newbie and a Hardcore in the game Dota 1
source_sentences.A0: The gamers are players, the nickname is given due to their love of video games, there are categories that characterize gamers: Newbie is the player who is starting to play videogames, Hardcore are who already have knowledge previous of the game and know what is the theme of the same and Professional who are the most experienced players who participate in international tournaments and promoting certain brands.
source_sentences.A1: It is known that each category of gamers provides a different brain interaction, because of that it is required to know what is the clearest difference by comparing 2 gamers, a Newbie and a Hardcore.
source_sentences.A2: It took data from gamers, a Newbie and a Hardcore to know their brain interaction for this was used Cyton and Daysi Boards that are devices capable of receiving brain data, in addition to using the connection 10-20 for the placement of the electrodes, being these 16 channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, C4, T5, T6, O1, O2, F7, F8, F3, F4, T3, T4, P3 and P4).
source_sentences.A3: The obtaining data was when the gamers were playing DOTA 1, having 22 minutes analyzed in both parts, with a sampling frequency of 250 and obtaining 128 data per second.
source_sentences.A4: Having as a result that in the channels F7 and P3 in the frequencies of 1 and 2 Hz a difference of signals, due to their separation indicating the difference of the cerebral interaction of the players, showing that the hardcore brainwave has more potential than the newbie brainwave in those channels.

source_sentences.T0: Syntax-Infused Variational Autoencoder for Text Generation
source_sentences.A0: We present a syntax-infused variational autoencoder (SIVAE), that integrates sentences with their syntactic trees to improve the grammar of generated sentences.
source_sentences.A1: Distinct from existing VAE-based text generative models, SIVAE contains two separate latent spaces, for sentences and syntactic trees.
source_sentences.A2: The evidence lower bound objective is redesigned correspondingly, by optimizing a joint distribution that accommodates two encoders and two decoders.
source_sentences.A3: SIVAE works with long short-term memory architectures to simultaneously generate sentences and syntactic trees.
source_sentences.A4: Two versions of SIVAE are proposed: one captures the dependencies between the latent variables through a conditional prior network, and the other treats the latent variables independently such that syntactically-controlled sentence generation can be performed.
source_sentences.A5: Experimental results demonstrate the generative superiority of SIVAE on both reconstruction and targeted syntactic evaluations.
source_sentences.A6: Finally, we show that the proposed models can be used for unsupervised paraphrasing given different syntactic tree templates.

source_sentences.T0: Linked knowledge sources for topic classification of microposts: A semantic graph-based approach
source_sentences.A0: AbstractShort text messages a.k.a Microposts (e.g. Tweets) have proven to be an effective channel for revealing information about trends and events, ranging from those related to Disaster (e.g. hurricane Sandy) to those related to Violence (e.g. Egyptian revolution).
source_sentences.A1: Being informed about such events as they occur could be extremely important to authorities and emergency professionals by allowing such parties to immediately respond.In this work we study the problem of topic classification (TC) of Microposts, which aims to automatically classify short messages based on the subject(s) discussed in them.
source_sentences.A2: The accurate TC of Microposts however is a challenging task since the limited number of tokens in a post often implies a lack of sufficient contextual information.In order to provide contextual information to Microposts, we present and evaluate several graph structures surrounding concepts present in linked knowledge sources (KSs).
source_sentences.A3: Traditional TC techniques enrich the content of Microposts with features extracted only from the Microposts content.
source_sentences.A4: In contrast our approach relies on the generation of different weighted semantic meta-graphs extracted from linked KSs.
source_sentences.A5: We introduce a new semantic graph, called category meta-graph.
source_sentences.A6: This novel meta-graph provides a more fine grained categorisation of concepts providing a set of novel semantic features.
source_sentences.A7: Our findings show that such category meta-graph features effectively improve the performance of a topic classifier of Microposts.Furthermore our goal is also to understand which semantic feature contributes to the performance of a topic classifier.
source_sentences.A8: For this reason we propose an approach for automatic estimation of accuracy loss of a topic classifier on new, unseen Microposts.
source_sentences.A9: We introduce and evaluate novel topic similarity measures, which capture the similarity between the KS documents and Microposts at a conceptual level, considering the enriched representation of these documents.Extensive evaluation in the context of Emergency Response (ER) and Violence Detection (VD) revealed that our approach outperforms previous approaches using single KS without linked data and Twitter data only up to 31.4% in terms of F1 measure.
source_sentences.A10: Our main findings indicate that the new category graph contains useful information for TC and achieves comparable results to previously used semantic graphs.
source_sentences.A11: Furthermore our results also indicate that the accuracy of a topic classifier can be accurately predicted using the enhanced text representation, outperforming previous approaches considering content-based similarity measures.

source_sentences.T0: Language design methods based on semantic principles
source_sentences.A0: Two language design methods based on principles derived from the denotational approach to programming language semantics are described and illustrated by an application to the language Pascal.
source_sentences.A1: The principles are, firstly, the correspondence between parametric and declarative mechanisms, and secondly, a principle of abstraction for programming languages adapted from set theory.
source_sentences.A2: Several useful extensions and generalizations of Pascal emerge by applying these principles, including a solution to the array parameter problem, and a modularization facility.

source_sentences.T0: New Models of the Generalized Minimum Spanning Tree Problem
source_sentences.A0: We consider a generalization of the Minimum Spanning Tree Problem, called the Generalized Minimum Spanning Tree Problem, denoted by GMST.
source_sentences.A1: It is known that the GMST problem is NP-hard.
source_sentences.A2: We present a stronger result regarding its complexity, namely, the GMST problem is NP-hard even on trees as well an exact exponential time algorithm for the problem based on dynamic programming.
source_sentences.A3: We describe new mixed integer programming models of the GMST problem, mainly containing a polynomial number of constraints.
source_sentences.A4: We establish relationships between the polytopes corresponding to their linear relaxations.
source_sentences.A5: Based on a new model of the GMST we present a solution procedure that solves the problem to optimality for graphs with nodes up to 240.
source_sentences.A6: We discuss the advantages of our method in comparison with earlier methods.
